result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B gives units once in the headers (kg, USD), right-aligns its numbers with consistent separators, and marks missing values with a dash placeholder plus a key that explains it. A repeats 'kg' and '$' in every cell. In A's CF-2213 row, the inline 'not yet quoted' note pushes $0.00 out of line with the rest of the cost column, and that row also shows a misleading $0.00. Both have light, easy-to-scan row rules; A's status pills are nicer to look at. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A puts the units once in the headers (Weight (kg), Cost (USD)), right-aligns the numbers with consistent separators, and uses one em-dash placeholder style for the missing ETA and cost. B repeats 'kg' and '$' in every cell. B also shows the unquoted cost as '$0.00' with a side note, which breaks the cost column's right alignment and suggests a real zero value. B's status badges look nice, but A fits the rubric better.
